title: Handle partial reads from a Linux serial port
description: A Linux service assumes each read() returns one complete UART packet. Explain why this fails and design a bounded incremental parser with timeout handling and reconnection. Address short reads, EINTR, nonblocking I/O, and malformed input.
prompt: A Linux service assumes each read() returns one complete UART packet. Explain why this fails and design a bounded incremental parser with timeout handling and reconnection. Address short reads, EINTR, nonblocking I/O, and malformed input.
constraints: State assumptions and separate measurements from guarantees.
rubric: Treat the serial port as a byte stream.
Retain incomplete state with bounded memory and framing rules.
Differentiate transient errors, EOF/device removal, and protocol errors.
follow_ups: How would you test without physical hardware?
How do termios settings affect this design?
hints: Write down the boundary cases before choosing an implementation.
Use explicit integer widths and keep intermediate values in range.
